title: Screen larger final merge application buffers
question: Does 256 KiB per final run improve a hard-capped terminal Uniform merge using the same file policy and fan-in?
summary: 256 KiB buffers increased complete-job elapsed 4.81% and CPU 4.69%. All three pairs regressed on both measures. Managed spill bytes and merge count matched. File-cache refaults rose 11.58%.

workloads: Exact 8 GiB terminal Uniform then Balanced(8), 197 initial runs and one last merge, m256, one worker, 1 GiB cgroup no swap.

validation.summary: Matched full field/ID/quotas/caps/cleanup verification in all pairs. Linux storage and admission controls, compact spill compile, instrumented 512 MiB coverage of both larger reads and 64 KiB fallback.

limitations: WSL2/ext4, one fixture and one worker. Cgroup page counters are scope observations with uncontrolled backing caches.
Test holds kernel read-ahead, 197-run merge order, and the raw spill format steady. It does not establish a universal optimal buffer size.
exclusions: Small/full warmups and read syscall probe jobs excluded. Fixture hashing and independent full output oracle outside clock.
reopen_when: Investigate a changed locality or file layout with measured per-reader refill cost or substantially different active run structure.
